title: Massive expansion and cryopreservation of functional human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes
protocol: Maintain hiPSCs under feeder-free conditions with daily medium changes and keep them at 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2.
Passage hiPSCs when they reach 80%-90% confluence (typically about 3 to 4 days after passaging).
Prewarm E8 medium, EDTA Dissociation Buffer, and Matrigel-coated plates to 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the medium from hiPSCs in each well of a 6-well culture plate.
Add 1 ml of 0.5 mM EDTA/PBS to each well containing hiPSCs.
Incubate the plate for 3-5 minutes.
Aspirate the EDTA and flush the hiPSCs with 1 ml of E8 + 5 μM Y27632.
Gently mix 2-5 times using a 1 ml tip to detach all cells.
Add required cell amount from the 1 ml suspension into each well of Matrigel-coated plates containing 2 ml E8 + 5 μM Y27632 (split ratio of 1:13).
Place the plate in the incubator and make side-to-side movements to equally disperse cells.
Prewarm hiPSC E8 Medium to 20°C–25°C each day.
Aspirate the medium and add 2 ml fresh prewarmed hiPSC E8 complete medium per well daily.
When hiPSCs reach 80%-90% confluence, they are ready for differentiation.
Prepare 3 mL/well of 37°C-preheated CM differentiation medium with the appropriate concentration of CHIR per hiPSC line.
Aspire the E8 medium and replace carefully with 3 mL/well with the prepared differentiation medium.
Do not re-freeze and thaw CHIR aliquots due to instability after thawing and freezing.
On day 1, carefully add 2 mL/well of preheated CM differentiation medium on top of the original medium.
Place the plate back into the 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2 incubator.
On day 2, carefully add 1 mL/well of preheated CM differentiation medium on top of the original medium.
Place the plate back into the 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2 incubator.
Aspirate the old medium.
Add 3 mL/well of 37°C-preheated CM differentiation medium with 2 μM Wnt-C59 to each well of the 6-well plate.
Place the plate back into the 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2 incubator.
Remove dead cell debris by shaking and aspirating the medium completely during differentiation.
Aspirate the medium on day 5.
Add 3 mL/well of 37°C-preheated CM differentiation medium to each well.
Place the plate back into the 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2 incubator.
Aspirate the medium on day 7.
Add 3 mL/well of 37°C-preheated CM culture medium to each well.
Place the plate back into the 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2 incubator.
Aspirate the medium on day 9.
Add 2 mL/well of 37°C-preheated CM purification medium (PM) to each well.
Place the plate back into the 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2 incubator.
Observe the amount of beating cardiomyocytes in each well under the bright field microscope.
Select wells where a beating percentage between 50% and 90% is observed.
Aspirate the medium from selected wells.
Wash the cells with PBS.
Incubate hiPSC-CMs with pure TrypLE Select (10×) for 15–45 min at 37°C.
Incubate hiPSC-CMs for approximately 15 minutes.
Gently shake the flask to detach the cells.
If necessary, repeat the incubation process up to two additional times (up to a total of 45 minutes).
Add 1.5 mL of warm RPMI-1640 per 75-cm² flask and distribute it evenly over the surface until all cells are detached.
Gently mix the cell suspension using a 5 mL pipette 2 to 5 times.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 1 mL of preheated CM replating medium per flask.
Count the cell suspension using Trypan Blue Solution and a counting machine.
Replate passage 1 (P1) hiPSC-CMs into culture flasks or plates with a split ratio of 1:10 to 1:20.
Add preheated CM replating medium according to the volume specified in Table 1.
Put the flask into the incubator.
Set incubator conditions to 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2, and 90% humidity.
Distribute cells by moving the flask in short side-to-side and back-and-forth motions.
Aspirate the medium from hiPSC-CMs after reaching 70%–80% confluency.
Wash hiPSC-CMs with PBS.
Add 3 mL of warm TrypLE per 75-cm² growth surface and incubate for 10-15 min at 37°C.
Detatch hiPSC-CMs by gently mixing with preheated RPMI-1640 using a pipette.
Transfer the cell suspension to a new 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of preheated splitting medium supplemented with optimal CHIR concentration per tube.
Count the resuspended cell suspension.
If cell numbers are high, use a larger volume of medium before counting.
Add preheated CM splitting medium to hiPSC-CMs according to density and volume as specified.
Remove Matrigel solution from new flasks.
Immediately add the cell solution to prepared culture flasks/plates.
Place the flask in the incubator.
Distribute cells by moving the flask side-to-side and back-and-forth.
Set incubator conditions to 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2, and 90% humidity.
Refresh expansion medium every other day according to volume specified.
After 5–8 days, passage hiPSC-CMs when they reach 70%–80% confluency.
Repeat steps for passages 2 through 5 as needed.
By each passage, split the hiPSC-CMs in a ratio and flasks according to specifications.
Count the hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes after dissociation as described in the Replating section.
Transfer the desired cell suspension for freezing to a 15-mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the CM in STEMdiff Cardiomyocyte Freezing Medium using 0.5 mL medium for 0.5–2 × 10^6 CMs and 1 mL of freezing medium for 2–8 × 10^6 CMs per vial.
Keep the cell suspension on ice.
Freeze the vials at −80°C for a minimum of 4 h and a maximum of 12 h in a CoolCell or 2-propanol-filled freezing container.
Transfer the vials to liquid nitrogen or −150°C for long-term storage.
Prepare 9 mL of 37°C-preheated RPMI medium in a 15-mL tube on room temperature.
Prepare a Matrigel-coated T75 per 3–6 × 10^6 or a T175 for 7–14 × 10^6 hiPSC-CMs.
Collect the vial with hiPSC-CMs from liquid nitrogen and thaw the cells at 37°C until only a little clump is visible.
Do not thaw more than three vials of CMs at one time.
Transfer the cell suspension to the 15-mL tube drop by drop while swirling the tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the hiPSC-CMs in the desired volume of CM thawing medium.
Count the cells within the cell suspension.
Aspirate the liquid from the Matrigel-coated flasks.
Seed the CMs into the Matrigel-coated flasks according to Table 1.
Put the flask into the incubator.
Move the flask in short side-to-side and back-and-forth motions to distribute the cells.
Set the incubator conditions to 37°C, 5% CO2, 21% O2, and 90% humidity.
Replace the thawing medium with CM expansion medium the next day.
Collect, fix, and immunocytochemically stain hiPSC-CMs for α-actinin and ki67 expression.
Dissociate the CMs as described in the Replating of differentiated hiPSC-CMs section.
Count the hiPSC-CMs and collect 100,000 cells from the cell suspension in 1.5 ml tubes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant and add 50 μl of 4% PFA.
Incubate for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant and add 1 ml PBS.
Transfer the cell suspension to a FACS tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 4°C for 3 min at 200 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend 1 × 10^5 cells in 50 μL of permeabilization buffer containing 5% BSA and 0.3% Triton X-100.
Incubate the cells for 30 min at 4°C.
Resuspend in 50 μL of flow cytometry buffer containing the α-actinin antibody (1:300 dilution) and ki67 antibody (1:200).
In another FACS tube, resuspend 1 × 10^5 cells in 50 μL of flow cytometry buffer with the respective isotype control (e.g., FITC mouse IgM, κ isotype at a 1:200 dilution).
Incubate the cells for 30 min at 4°C.
Wash the cells with 2.5 mL of flow cytometry buffer and centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat washing two more times.
Resuspend in 50 μL of flow cytometry buffer containing the secondary-antibody Goat-anti-mouse (1:300 dilution) and Goat-anti-rabbit (1:300 dilution).
Analyze the cells with a flow cytometer.
